about.heading: One question, three different doors.
paragraphs: I was studying medicine in Cuba, at the University of Medical Sciences in Pinar del Río — near the top of my class, with a clear path ahead. Circumstances at home forced me to leave before finishing: two years done, a plan interrupted.

I arrived in the United States without fluent English. I waited tables while teaching myself the language. I earned my Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) certification while still working — and found a new door back to the same calling: helping people function and be understood.

Leaving medicine didn't mean leaving the reason I wanted to be a doctor. I've kept following that same pattern — not waiting for the right degree or the right permission, I've been teaching myself UX design and AI and applying it to real projects. Self-taught English, then RBT certification while waiting tables, and now UX and AI on my own while working as an RBT. The same mission, rebuilt.
